The account of the young earth-
quake felt here is explained by the 
South Bend Tribune of Friday, as fol-
lows:
From the reports made hy persons 
visiting the late wreck near Laporte, 
it is the conclusion that it was the ex 
plosion of dynamite that produced the 
much talked ot earthquake. After the 
collision many parties belonging in the 
neighborhood repaired to. the scene, 
some standing upon the bridge and 
others on the ground about the wreck, 
hut when the explosion occurred no 
one-could be seen; everybody was 
blown prostrate to the ground. Some 
pieces oi the wreck were picked up on 
Bald Hill, several miles south o'f the 
place of disaster. Tne great wonder 
is, ho ore was killed. The car contain-
ing the explosive material was, but a 
moment before tlie explosion, surround-
ed by people, when an order as if from 
heaven came, to quickly disperse, and 
no sooner had they scattered when the 
awful explosion took place, quaking 
the earth for fifty miles around.
The Laporte Argus says' that soon 
after the collision several tanks filled 
with coal oil' sprung aleak, and the 
burning fluid ran over the wrecked 
cars, setting them on fire. One of the 
box cars in the wreck was loaded with 
merchandise, consisting in part of hard-
ware, clothing, tar in cans, etc., and 
among the other things was evidently 
a quantity of powder or dynamite. 
While the people were standing around 
viewing the wreck, there was a terrific 
explosion that scattered that general 
merchandise to the four winds of heav-
en and strewed the ground with divers 
and sundry articles for a mile each 
way. Fortunately nobody was hurt. 
The explosion broke many of the win-
dows in the neighborhood, some of 
them being a full mile away. It tore 
the track and ground up and scattered 
things around promiscuously. The 
farmers are picking up a liberal sup-
ply of wrenches, bolts etc., one half 
mile from the wreck. The net logs to 
tlie railroad is two new locomotives' 
and fifteen cars with their contents, 
and it will amount to a heavy sum.
